'''John Hubert Thompson''' (June 19, 1951 – May 9, 2025) was an American [[statistician]] and [[Director of the United States Census Bureau]].<ref>[https://www.census.gov/newsroom/bios/john-thompson.html John H. Thompson: Director, U.S. Census Bureau]. Bio on US Census web site. Version of 13 Jan 2015.</ref><ref>[https://www.census.gov/newsroom/blogs/director/2017/06/farewell_from_johnt.html Director's Blog: Farewell], 30 June 2017</ref> In this position, one of his main duties was to oversee preparations for the [[2020 United States census]]. On May 9, 2017, the [[Commerce Department]] announced that he would leave his post on June 30.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Bahrampour|first1=Tara|title=U.S. Census director resigns amid turmoil over funding of 2020 count|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/social-issues/us-census-director-resigns-amid-turmoil-over-funding-of-2020-count/2017/05/09/8f8657c6-34ea-11e7-b412-62beef8121f7_story.html|newspaper=Washington Post|date=May 9, 2017}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Thompson was born in [[Washington, D.C.]] on June 19, 1951.<ref>{{cite web|title=John Hubert Thompson|date=May 16, 2025|website=[[Legacy.com]]|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/legacyremembers/john-thompson-obituary?id=58410661|accessdate=May 20, 2025}}</ref> He received [[B.S.]] and [[M.S.]] degrees in mathematics from [[Virginia Tech|Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University]] in 1973 and 1975, respectively.<ref>[http://www.vtnews.vt.edu/articles/2013/11/112613-science-distinction.html College of Science enshrines first class to Hall of Distinction]. ''Virginia Tech News'' site. 26 Nov 2013.</ref> After graduation, he spent 27 years working at the [[United States Census Bureau]], retiring in 2002 after holding the position of associate director, where he was responsible for the [[2000 United States census|2000 Census]]. Prior to that, Thompson served as Chief of the Decennial Management Division. He worked in the Statistical Support Division from 1987 to 1995 and the Statistical Methods Division from 1975 to 1987.

From 2008 to 2013, Thompson was the President and [[Chief Executive Officer|CEO]] of [[NORC at the University of Chicago]]. Thompson joined NORC in 2002 as the executive vice president for survey operations and was appointed president and CEO in 2008.

He was confirmed by the [[United States Senate]] to be the 24th Census Bureau director on August 1, 2013.<ref>[https://www.census.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2013/cb13-141.html Thompson Confirmed as Census Bureau Director]. Census Bureau web site. 2 Aug 2013.</ref>

Thompson died in [[Bend, Oregon]] on May 9, 2025, at the age of 73.<ref>{{cite news|title=Former US Census Bureau director John Thompson, who guided preparations for 2020 head count, dies|website=[[Associated Press]]|date=May 19, 2025|url=https://apnews.com/article/census-bureau-norc-john-thompson-4e8570b8421d19501354d2d13dab5a14|accessdate=May 20, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Jarmin |first1=Ron S. |title=Remembering John H. Thompson |url=https://www.census.gov/newsroom/blogs/director/2025/05/remembering-john-h-thompson.html?utm_campaign=&utm_content=&utm_medium=email&utm_source=govdelivery |website=Census.gov |publisher=U.S. Census Bureau |access-date=16 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref>
